extra.message: CSV Injection via User-Controlled Fields in Export Reports — An attacker may achieve remote code execution or data exfiltration when an administrator or manager opens the exported CSV in a spreadsheet application like Microsoft Excel. [verified: No sanitization of CSV metacharacters (e.g., '=', '+', '-', '@') exists in csv_response or upstream; tenant.full_name and tenant.email come directly from user profile updates and are written unescaped into the CSV, enabling formula injection when an admin opens the exported file.]

Server-Side Request Forgery in Tenant Relay Probe — An attacker can probe internal services (e.g., cloud metadata endpoints, database interfaces, internal APIs), potentially exfiltrating sensitive data or facilitating lateral movement. [verified: The endpoint parameter (line 79) is directly passed to urllib.request.urlopen (line 80) without any validation or sanitization, allowing an attacker to supply internal URLs (e.g., cloud metadata). No compensating controls are present in the shown code; the route is reachable unauthenticated via query parameter.]

Inverted authorization check in document upload for non-lease entities — An attacker can upload arbitrary documents to any entity they are not authorized to access, potentially leading to unauthorized file storage, stored XSS (if documents are served with unsafe content types), or information disclosure. [verified: In _validate_document_scope, for non-lease entities, require_forbidden(can_access_document(...)) is inverted: it passes (allows upload) when can_access_document returns False, thereby bypassing entity-level access control for admin/manager users. However, the upload endpoint requires admin/manager roles, limiting the exploitation to those privileged users.]

Information Disclosure via Unrestricted User Listing for Maintenance Workers — An authenticated user with a role other than property_admin can enumerate all maintenance worker users, disclosing their full names and email addresses, which may aid social engineering or targeted attacks. [verified: The authorization check on line 24 only denies access if `role != 'maintenance_worker'` when the current user is not a property admin, so any authenticated user can obtain a list of maintenance workers (including email and full name) by passing `role=maintenance_worker`. No additional validation or role-specific scoping exists to prevent this disclosure, and the endpoint is fully reachable.]
